purpose: Reconciliation checklist, not runtime catalog input or an automatic import instruction.

authoritative_sources.selection: storage/knowledge/authority.json; JSON seeds before migration, SQLite afterward
authoritative_sources.managed_documents: categories, parameters, category_parameters, operations, operation_parameters, operation_rules, template_bindings, context_rules
authoritative_sources.schemas: Shared types plus operation mappings/rules; compiled release artifacts; legacy schema.json retained as migration evidence
authoritative_sources.runtime: storage/catalog_releases/active.json pins immutable metadata, schemas, templates and retrieval

compatibility_policy.machine_ids: Preserve existing IDs; change labels instead. ID changes require an explicit later migration.
compatibility_policy.payload_keys: Preserve existing parameter paths and representations.
compatibility_policy.new_operations: No target-document operations were imported or activated in Phases 1-5.

completed_membership_backfill.source: Existing operation schema properties and explicit x-parameter-id references only
completed_membership_backfill.scope: Current six categories only; new domain definitions still require review
completed_membership_backfill.repeat_policy: Preview shows the schema-used subset; never automatically replace reviewed memberships or remove unused definitions

completed_operation_backfill.source: Authoritative legacy schemas, current operation versions, and reviewed category memberships
completed_operation_backfill.runtime_policy: Historical Phase 3 comparison-only milestone; superseded by the registry promotion below.
completed_operation_backfill.promotion: Phase 4 promoted the reviewed records after equivalence checks.

completed_schema_publication.authoring_authority: Selected backend; this workspace migrated to SQLite
completed_schema_publication.runtime: Immutable release metadata, compiled schemas, templates and matching retrieval index; inventory/planned context remains separately revisioned
completed_schema_publication.initial_publication: Indexed baseline activated; SQLite publication recorded in docs/KNOWLEDGE_EVOLUTION_COMPLETION.md

completed_json_management.storage: Revision-checked local JSON with exclusive writer lock, audit journal and rollback/recovery
completed_json_management.database_cutover: Historical JSON-only milestone; superseded by approved SQLite completion
completed_json_management.scope: Metadata, memberships, scoped operation contracts, previews, validation, import/export and explicit publication; no server or GUI

completed_sqlite_management.authority: Single explicit pointer, no JSON fallback after cutover
completed_sqlite_management.safety: Foreign keys, transaction/audit atomicity, generation revisions, stale-write checks, dependency protections and recoverable authority switch
completed_sqlite_management.equivalence: Identical catalog documents and typed records; shared management contract tests against both stores

pending_decisions.decision_needed: Supply the missing parameter types; define array item structures, enum choices, and units as operation contracts. Do not infer types from names.
Review definitions and category membership before any import.
Choose one canonical behavior owner with discovery aliases, or document different semantics.
Keep BGP and IS-IS although absent from the target. Review expansion from ip_address to Interface without silently moving existing operations.

Use scoped mappings only after semantic review. Prefix/netmask and admin_up/admin_state require validated conversions. Preserve OSPF interfaces as objects, not strings. Route preference is not route metric; action/mode may mean different things across domains.
Do not equate compound configure_ospf with enable_ospf_process, exact-next-hop route removal with deletion by prefix, or exact-address removal with all-address removal.
Retain existing vendor overlays, including Cisco/Huawei OSPF process IDs and Juniper VLAN names/BGP peer groups, until reviewed replacement contracts exist.

deferred: Vendor-device certification and broad model-quality benchmarking
